          "text": "# Beta Vol: An Orange Beacon in Volans\n\n*This southern-sky giant is easy to overlook in a dim constellation, but its brightness and measured motion give observers plenty to look for.*\n\nIn the faint southern constellation Volans, Beta Vol offers a useful reminder that a star\u2019s apparent stillness is only an illusion. It shines at about magnitude 3.76\u2014bright enough for the unaided eye under a reasonably dark sky\u2014and lies roughly 108 light-years away. In telescope or binoculars, it is not a dramatic double-star showpiece; the appeal is the star itself, a nearby giant whose catalogue measurements reveal both its nature and its slow drift across the sky.\n\nSIMBAD lists Beta Vol as a K2III star. The \u201cK2\u201d marks a star cooler than the Sun, with the warm, orange hue associated with K-type stars; \u201cIII\u201d identifies it as a giant.
